title: OpenClaw for GTM: Give Your Agent Prospecting, Enrichment and Outbound Skills
summary: OpenClaw and Hermes run on your machine, answer in Slack or WhatsApp, and load skills from ClawHub. What they lack is GTM data and the provider accounts behind it. How to install Cargo's skills in both, sign the agent in, schedule a weekly list, and when the job should move off the agent and into a play.
body_markdown:
**OpenClaw can already do go-to-market work. It just has nothing to do it with.** It runs on your own machine, answers you in Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp or iMessage, schedules its own jobs and loads skills that follow the AgentSkills standard. Ask it to find fifty heads of RevOps at Series B fintechs and it will open a browser, search, and hand you a list that is half guesses, because it has no B2B data, no email verification and no account at any provider that has either.


That is the gap Cargo’s skills fill. Install them and the same request runs against licensed data providers through one CLI, with verified emails, a cost receipt and a record of the run. The skills are on ClawHub under` @cargo-ai` , they work the same way in Hermes Agent, and a new Cargo account starts with 100 free credits and no card.


## What the skills give your agent#


Two packs, both public and both published to ClawHub on every change.


**The platform pack (19 skills).** One skill per Cargo domain:` cargo-gtm` for sourcing, enrichment, scoring and outreach drafts,` cargo-storage` for querying your data,` cargo-orchestration` for running workflows and batches,` cargo-mailbox-management` for sending,` cargo-diagnostics` for explaining a run that went wrong, and a router skill,` cargo` , that tells the agent which of the others to load.


**The job pack (37 skills).** Each named for the job rather than for Cargo, so the agent finds it by what you asked:` find-work-email` ,` build-tam-list` ,` find-stakeholders` ,` track-job-changes` ,` track-funding-rounds` ,` find-companies-using-tech` ,` verify-email-list` ,` score-leads` ,` research-account` . The skills carry the procedure, not the data. The data comes from the providers Cargo connects to, which is why every skill needs the` cargo-ai` CLI and a signed-in workspace.


## Install in OpenClaw#


Install the CLI first. OpenClaw checks each skill’s requirements, and a Cargo skill without` cargo-ai` on the path stays installed but hidden:` openclaw skills info cargo-gtm` reports **Needs setup** and **Visible to model: no** until the binary exists.


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli


openclaw   skills   install   @cargo-ai/cargo
openclaw   skills   install   @cargo-ai/cargo-gtm
openclaw   skills   install   @cargo-ai/find-work-email


```


That installs into the current agent’s workspace. Add` --global` to share the skills across agents. To take the whole platform pack in one command instead of one skill at a time:


shellscript


```text
npx   skills   add   getcargohq/cargo-skills   --agent   openclaw   -g


```


Check that the agent can see them:


shellscript


```text
openclaw   skills   info   cargo-gtm     # ✓ Ready, Visible to model: yes


```


OpenClaw’s own guidance applies to these as to any third-party skill: read it before you enable it. Every skill is plain markdown, and the source is in[getcargohq/cargo-skills](https://github.com/getcargohq/cargo-skills) and[getcargohq/gtm-skills](https://github.com/getcargohq/gtm-skills) .


## Sign the agent in#


Sign-up runs entirely in the terminal and creates the account on first use, so there is no separate sign-up step:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com                   # sends a code, then exits
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com   --code   123456
cargo-ai   whoami


```


Do this on the machine that runs the OpenClaw gateway, because that is where the skills execute. On a box that runs unattended, use an API token instead of your personal session: create one under **Settings → API** , scoped to one workspace, and give the gateway` CARGO_API_TOKEN` . A saved login acts as you across every workspace you belong to. A token can be scoped down and revoked from the dashboard.


The 100 free credits come to roughly 5,000 leads sourced, 1,000 verified-email enrichments, or 50 fully enriched contacts.


## What to ask it#


Ask the way you would ask a colleague, from whichever channel the agent lives in. The skills’ triggers are written in that voice:


- “Find 50 heads of RevOps at Series B fintechs in France.”
- “Find work emails for the people in this CSV.”
- “Who on our customer list changed jobs this month?”
- “Which companies in this list use Snowflake?”
- “Research Acme before my call and give me a brief with sources.”


The agent loads the router, picks the skill, and runs the job through the CLI, and each run reports what it spent.


The skills also carry the rules for anything that touches a person. Every step that contacts someone is gated on a consent basis, a suppression list and a volume limit, and purchased or scraped lists and consumer targeting are refused. An agent with Cargo’s skills drafts outreach for your sequencer or for a Cargo mailbox. It does not bulk-mail strangers because someone asked it to in a group chat.


## Put it on a schedule#


OpenClaw’s built-in scheduler turns a request into a standing one. A list every Monday morning, delivered to a Slack channel:


shellscript


```text
openclaw   automations   create   "0 8 * * 1"   \
"Using the Cargo skills, find companies in our ICP that raised a round in the last 7 days, find the head of sales at each, and post the list with verified emails."   \
--name   "Monday funded accounts"   \
--tz   "Europe/Paris"   \
--session   isolated   \
--announce   --channel   slack   --to   "channel:C1234567890"


```


This is the right shape for a job one person wants, delivered to them, where a missed week costs nothing.


## When the job should leave the agent#


A personal agent runs on one person’s machine, with that person’s session, until the laptop closes. That is fine for the Monday list. It stops being fine when the job has to run whether or not that machine is on, when the team depends on its output, or when someone has to answer for what it did six weeks ago.


At that point the agent should stop running the job and start building it. The same CLI declares the work as a Cargo play, in TypeScript, in a repository: it runs on Cargo on its schedule or when data changes, retries on failure, and leaves a trace of every run.


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   project   init   my-gtm   --cookbook   new-hire-detection
cd   my-gtm
npm   install                 # the cookbook's dependencies
cargo-ai   project   plan       # the diff against the workspace
cargo-ai   project   deploy     # needs a login


```


Ask OpenClaw to do it, with the` cargo-project` skill loaded, and it will. That is the division of labour that holds up: the agent drafts and changes the system, Cargo holds the credentials, the data, the schedule and the audit log, and a person approves the diff. We wrote up the operating model in[run GTM with coding agents](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/run-gtm-with-coding-agents) .


## Hermes Agent#


Hermes Agent, from Nous Research, follows the same AgentSkills standard, so the same packs work. The skills CLI installs them into Hermes’s skill directory:


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
npx   skills   add   getcargohq/cargo-skills   --agent   hermes-agent   -g     # → ~/.hermes/skills


```


Sign in the same way, on the machine Hermes runs on. If you are moving from OpenClaw,` hermes claw migrate` imports the skills you already installed there.


## Frequently asked questions#


Yes, with the right skills. On its own OpenClaw can browse and search, but it has no B2B contact data or email verification. Cargo’s skills give it sourcing, enrichment, verification and scoring against licensed data providers through the` cargo-ai` CLI, with a cost receipt for every run.


Install the CLI with` npm install -g @cargo-ai/cli` , then run` openclaw skills install @cargo-ai/cargo-gtm` for each skill you want, or` npx skills add getcargohq/cargo-skills --agent openclaw -g` for the whole platform pack. Install the CLI first: without it OpenClaw marks the skills as needing setup and hides them from the model.


The skill declares` cargo-ai` as a required binary and OpenClaw cannot find it on the path. Run` npm install -g @cargo-ai/cli` on the machine that runs the gateway, then` openclaw skills info cargo-gtm` should report Ready.


Yes. Hermes follows the same AgentSkills standard.` npx skills add getcargohq/cargo-skills --agent hermes-agent -g` installs the pack into` ~/.hermes/skills` , and the CLI and sign-in are the same as for OpenClaw.


The skills are free and open source. A new Cargo account starts with 100 free credits and needs no card, which covers roughly 5,000 leads sourced, 1,000 verified-email enrichments or 50 fully enriched contacts. Paid plans are usage-based with no seats.


It can draft outreach and hand it to your sequencer or a Cargo mailbox, and every step that touches a person is gated on a consent basis, a suppression list and a volume limit. Bulk unsolicited messaging, purchased or scraped lists and consumer targeting are refused by the skills themselves.
